canonical_statement: If a first-order sentence phi semantically entails a sentence psi in one ambient language, then there is a sentence theta whose nonlogical symbols occur in both phi and psi, such that phi entails theta and theta entails psi.
domain_and_universes: FirstOrder.Language.{u,v}; sentences and structures in the associated mathlib universes; Prop
hypotheses: phi semantically entails psi in every nonempty L-structure
conclusion: There exists an L-sentence theta whose nonlogical symbols occur in both phi and psi, such that phi semantically entails theta and theta semantically entails psi.

alternate_encodings.target: four-language formulation with an explicit common sublanguage and joint language
alternate_encodings.relationship: expected equivalent only when the common sublanguage is proved to be the exact intersection of endpoint symbol occurrences
alternate_encodings.checked_witness: none; the historical candidate is not credited as a transport

excluded_degenerate_cases: No equality or disjointness of the side languages is assumed. Empty common languages and identical side languages remain included. Theory-relative, infinitary, propositional, and higher-order interpolation are outside this root.
foundation_profile: Classical first-order model theory over mathlib Language/Structure semantics; exact choice, quotient, and classical axiom closure remains open.
tcb_profile: Lean 4 kernel plus pinned mathlib; exact toolchain and dependency fingerprint remain open.
computation_profile: No computation, decision procedure, or oracle is credited at intake.
